taunt: I shot a spitball through a brick. Your face is softer than a brick.
The straw is bendy. The aim is not.
Extra sauce on everything. You are everything.
I talk through the straw. Everything sounds like a whistle. Including this threat.
The possum found a straw. The straw found a target. Hello.
Spit, aim, win. Not in that order. Spit is always first.
The mask is a wrapper. The holes are in the wrong place. I aim by sound.
I do not need to be close. I prefer not to be close. You smell like the pipe.
One straw. Infinite ammo. My mouth never runs dry.
The bend is taped straight. The tape is from a pizza box.
Lidd slaps. Napkin sweeps. Sporke pokes. I handle everything past arm's length.
Wet paper at terminal velocity. Science. Also gross.
Sauce on the slice, sauce on the straw, sauce in the spitball. It is a system.
Get closer. No, farther. I have a range and you are not it.
I can hit a fly at forty feet. You are bigger than a fly. Barely.
Hold your breath. I am holding mine. Mine comes out faster.
The wrapper says BENDY. The possum thought it was my name. We compromised.
Spitballs do not run out. Pride does. Yours is running.
I whistle when I breathe. You will whistle when I hit you.
The straw came with a soda. The soda is a memory. The straw is a legend.
Range is a gift. Spit is a talent. You are a target.
I charge the shot by puffing my cheeks. It looks silly. It hits like a brick.
Keep walking toward me. I like it when the math is easy.
I hit a rat from across the pipe once. The rat is fine. The rat respects me.
My brothers fight up close. I fight from the good seats.
Extra sauce is not a request. It is a worldview.
There is a fourth hole in the wrapper. It is for my ear. It is also wrong.
The spitball is paper. The paper was a menu. Order up.
I do not blink. The wrapper does not let me. Neither does the aim.
Cheeks full. Target spotted. Goodbye.
I can shoot around corners. I cannot see around corners. It works out.
You brought fists to a straw fight.
Lidd says the tray is sacred. The straw is holy. There is a difference. I will not explain it.
The possum trained me by throwing peanuts. I hit every peanut. He ate none.
Pizza sauce on the pizza is fine. Sauce on the crust is better. Sauce on you is best.
I breathe in. You go down. That is one breath.
My cheeks hold more than a bucket. Ask Napkin. He has the bucket.
Range check. Yes. You are in it. You were always in it.
The straw is not a weapon. The lung is a weapon. The straw is the barrel.
Spitball to the eye. Spitball to the other eye. Spitball to the pride.
Stop running at me. It only makes the shot more satisfying.
I taped the bend straight so the spit goes where I look. I look at you.
I have never lost a spit fight. I have never had a spit fight. Both true.
The wrapper mask was the possum's idea. The holes were his too. I forgive him daily.
Spit is free. The look on your face is the real cost.
Sporke says I am a coward. Sporke says it from across the room. Where I can hit him.
I do not throw things. Throwing is for geckos with arms worth using.
A wet wad of menu at the speed of a sneeze. That is the whole move.
My sauce ratio is two to one. Sauce to pizza. Sauce to you.
I shoot first and ask nothing. Questions are for close range.
I hit the moon once. It was a street light. It went out. Close enough.
Four geckos. I am the one who never gets hit. Today included.
The straw bends. I do not.
You are a big easy shape. I like big easy shapes.
I can spit through the straw, around the straw, and past the straw. The straw is a formality.
Everybody runs at me. Everybody arrives late.
I eat the pizza through the straw. Takes a while. I have time. You do not.
Rats scatter when I inhale. Smart rats.
The sewer is my shooting range. You walked onto it.
I hum through the straw when I aim. The tune is the last thing you hear. It is not a good tune.
Cheeks loaded. Wrapper on. Sauce ready. Fire.
You are at exactly the distance where I win.
I taught the rats to fetch spitballs. They refuse. Smart rats.
The holes in the wrapper line up with nothing. I still never miss.
Lidd found me under a lid. The possum found the straw next to me. We came as a set.
Napkin cleans up the spitballs. He has opinions. He keeps them.
If I inhale any harder the pipe will come with me.
I hit you from here. I hit you from there. I hit you from the credits.
The spitball has a name. It is Lunch.
Charge shot. Big wad. Say goodbye to your hat.
I have a tail for balance. The aim is all lung.
The straw was free. The lung was free. The spit is free. You get it all for nothing.
I spit in the sewer and a boat sank. Allegedly.
The possum cannot see past his nose. I can hit past the city.
Sauce on the floor. Sauce on the wall. Sauce on the gecko who did not dodge. Sauce.
The mask makes me look like I am asleep. I am never asleep. The straw has no off switch.
Walk into my range. Everybody does. It is a big range.
Distance is a friend. You are not.
I missed once. I was aiming at the thing behind you. I hit that too.
The straw has a bend, a tape, and a reputation.
You are standing where my last spitball landed. Look down. Yes. That.
I eat like a straw and fight like a cannon.
Napkin says I waste paper. Napkin folds his face. We are different.
I whistle before I fire. It is polite. It is also the last warning.
Aim is just caring where the spit goes. I care a lot.
The wrapper was pink and white. The pink is sauce now.
The crust is a handle. The straw is a weapon. The sauce is the point.
I have never run toward anything. Things run toward me and regret it.
I inhale, the rats hold on to something. You should too.
It is not spit. It is a projectile with a wet personality.
Point blank is a waste of a good straw. Stay there.
I was the last thing in the bag. The straw was under me. Fate.
My brothers get the glory. I get the clean shirt.
You cannot block spit. You can only regret the direction you faced.
Shoot, reload, shoot. Reload is a breath. I breathe a lot.
Your hat is a target. Your face is a bonus.
I do not need a tray, a mop, or two sporks. I need air.
Hold still. No. Move. I like the moving ones.
I hit the possum once. He played dead. He was already asleep. Hard to tell.
Spit happens.
continue: Extra sauce. On the continue. I do not care that it is a screen. Coin.
Lidd says pineapple. I say sauce. Sauce goes on pineapple too. Coin.
Insert a coin and I will put the straw down. For a second.
Napkin wants olives. Olives in sauce. Everyone wins. Coin.
I am down. The straw is up. Coin so they match.
Sporke says anchovies. Anchovies in sauce. See. Sauce fixes everything. Coin.
The possum wants plain. Plain is sauce with nothing on it. Coin.
Ten seconds. Extra sauce. One coin. Three words I say a lot.
No sauce, no continue. Those are my terms. Through a straw.
Whoever pays picks the topping. Sauce is not a topping. Sauce is the pizza. Coin.
A quarter and a bottle of sauce. Either works. Both is better.
I will get up for a coin. I will aim for free.
The spitball is loaded. The coin slot is not. Fix one of those.
Sauce on the crust, sauce on the box, sauce on the quarter. Insert it anyway.
One coin and I stop whistling. For a bit.
ending: Strawe put a spitball through the moon. The moon is fine. The spitball is still going.
Strawe won the toppings vote with extra sauce. The pizza was soup. He drank it through the straw.
The wrapper mask finally tore. The new wrapper had the holes in the right place. Strawe punched new ones.
Strawe hit every name in the credits with a spitball. Nobody asked him to.
The possum taped the straw's bend straight for good. It bent back by morning. Strawe prefers it.
Strawe opened a shooting range in the sewer. The targets are pizza boxes. The prize is sauce.
Kevin the rat learned to dodge spitballs. He is the only one.
Strawe beat 996 bootlegs without taking a hit. He took one during the credits. From Sporke. By accident.
The straw retired to the wall beside the tray and the mop. It whistles when the wind blows.
Strawe spat the last spitball into the sunset. It is still a sunset. It is also wet.
The Geckos' pizza place added a sauce fountain. Strawe guards it with the straw.
Strawe inhaled for the final shot and the sewer came with him. Napkin put it back.
